activity_context.topic_title: Properties of Variance for Discrete Random Variables

feedback.problem:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\text{E}[X]=0,$ calculate $\text{Var}[4X].$ 

| $x$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{3}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constant $a,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[aX]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=4.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[4X] & ={4}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =16\cdot \text{Var}[X].\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

Additionally, we're given that $\text{E}[X]=0.$ 

We start by computing $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & =(-1)^{2}\cdot f(-1)+{0}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{1}^{2}\cdot f(1) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{5} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}-{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[4X] & =16\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =16\cdot \frac{2}{5} \\  & =\frac{32}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
